subject: Request: C-suite approval for extended POC + billing term exception
messages:
From: Sophia Liang <sophia@regulate.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@regulate.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: POC extension and invoicing flexibility

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the private deployment options. We're close to a procurement window but hitting an internal timing mismatch: our security and budget approvals won't land until the end of July.

Two asks we hope you can help with:
- Can Redwood extend our POC window by 60 days beyond the standard PLG sandbox? The additional time is primarily for integration with our data team and an extra compliance review.
- Is there any way you can grant a one-time credit uplift (ideally ~50k token-equivalent) to cover expected test traffic while we finalize purchase orders? Also, our procurement team needs Net 45 invoice terms (standard is Net 30).

I've attached the security questionnaire and an updated scope doc for the POC. If we can secure these accommodations, we can commit to a scoped SOW and move to a paid dedicated pilot once procurement clears.

Appreciate your help — looping in Procurement for transparency.

Best,
Sophia Liang
Head of Platform Engineering
Regulate.ai

Attachments: Regulate_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, POC_Scope_v2.docx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Liang <sophia@regulate.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: POC extension and invoicing flexibility

Hi Sophia — great to hear the team is making progress and thanks for the clear ask.

We can support an extension and want to avoid blocking your procurement cycle. Proposed path:
- Extend POC by 60 days (one-time exception).
- Provide an upfront credit uplift to cover test traffic. I will need C-suite signoff for credits beyond our standard PLG allowance.
- Billing terms: Net 45 is a material change from standard terms; that will require (i) approval from Rev Ops and Finance and (ii) an exec exception.

I'll escalate internally with a concise justification and recommended concessions to speed approval. Can you confirm the PO target date (best estimate) and whether Regulate.ai is willing to sign a short SOW amendment that documents milestones and expected conversion criteria?

Thanks — I'll follow up as soon as I have an answer from my side.

— Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Request: POC extension and invoicing flexibility

Folks — forwarding Regulate.ai's request. TL;DR: regulated prospect needs a 60-day POC extension, asks for ~50k token-equivalent credits, and requests Net 45 payment terms to accommodate their purchase-order cadence. They will sign an SOW amendment tying milestones to conversion.

Why I think we should consider:
- Regulate.ai looks like a strategic expansion prospect for regulated verticals — if the POC proves out we have a clear path to a dedicated/private deployment with a multi-year contract.
- The customer has completed the security questionnaire and is ready to sign the SOW amendment; procurement timing is the blocker, not product fit.

My recommended concession package for executive signoff:
1) POC extension: 60 days (one-off).
2) Free credits: 50,000 token-equivalent uplift applied as sandbox/topup.
3) Billing term: grant Net 45 for the first paid invoice only (one-time exception) OR alternatively Net 30 with a 30-day invoice hold (if Finance prefers).

If approved, I'll require a one-page internal MakeGood (conversion commitment) and the SOW amendment signed prior to applying credits. Attaching the POC scope and the security questionnaire for context.

Attachments: POC_Scope_v2.docx, Regulate_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, Signed_SOW_stub.txt

Can you weigh in with approvals or changes? I can tighten the language for the exec note if you want.

— Jordan
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Request: POC extension and invoicing flexibility

Team — thanks for the summary, Jordan. Reviewed the attached docs and the HubSpot deal notes. My decision: approved with modifications.

Executive decision (one-time exception):
- Approve a 60-day POC extension.
- Approve a credits uplift, but limited to 25,000 token-equivalent (not the full 50k requested). This reduces our downside exposure while still removing an adoption roadblock.
- Do NOT approve a permanent Net 45 term. We will NOT change our standard T&C. However, we will allow a one-time billing accommodation: Net 30 terms with a 30-day invoice hold (Finance will not invoice until procurement confirms PO within that 30-day window). This effectively gives Regulate.ai operational breathing room without altering our contract baseline.

Conditions:
1) Customer signs the SOW amendment documenting milestones and a target conversion date.
2) Customer agrees to a conversion checkpoint at day 45 of the extended POC where an AE + CS health check is scheduled.
3) Credits are applied only after SOW execution and will be tracked in our billing ledger as a one-off promotional allowance.

Marissa/Aditya — please coordinate the credit application, update HubSpot (deal RGL-2027-0412), and notify Finance to prepare the one-time invoice-hold process. Jordan — communicate the decision to Sophia and capture explicit SOW signature before we apply credits.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
